newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt not planning to strip Eramet assets.
newsitem.headline: French govt not planning to strip Eramet assets.

text.p: France said on Tuesday it had no intention of stripping part of Eramet's mining assets in New Caledonia and that future negotiations over mining reserves in the French territory would respect "the rights and the social interests of all partners involved".

"As majority shareholder, the state gives, as any shareholder would, priority to the social interest of the company...It formally denies the serious allegations that it might try to rob Eramet of part of its mining resources," the French finance and industry ministries said in a joint statement.
"These rumours have sparked a brutal fall in the company stock," the statement said.
Shares in Eramet hit a year-low of 247 francs on Tuesday before rebounding by 19 francs to 285 francs after the government's statement.

Eramet share took a beating as investors worried the French government may force it to sell part of its mining assets in New Caledonia for political reasons, possibly ousting chairman Yves Rambaud in the process.

Rambaud opposes plans by local groups in new Caledonia and Canadian firm Falconbridge to build a nickel plant in northern new Caledonia, which would compete with Eramet's mines there, analysts have said.
The plan would deal a blow to Eramet's expansion strategy in New Caledonia as Eramet would have to part with some of the reserves of its Thiebaghi nickel deposit, they said.
In the statement, the French government said it planned to hold talks over the future usage of New-Caledonia's mining resources.
It said it hoped the talks would a "help better value the natural resources of New Caledonia and guarantee the long-term access to mining resources of current and future players".
Eramet board was also meeting today to study a proposed plan to turn Eramet into a company with a supervisory and a management board.
"The composition of the supervisory and management board will be reviewed in coming weeks," the statement only said.
"The state wishes that the new management teams will be selected for their ability to best defend the long-term interests of Eramet," it also said.
